title: Navigating Financial Success: Retirement Savings While Raising a Child with Developmental Disabilities
summary: Learn strategies for balancing retirement savings while raising a child with developmental disabilities, from special-needs trusts to long-term planning.
body_text: Navigating Financial Success: Retirement Savings While Raising a Child with Developmental Disabilities Published on July 22, 2026 | 3 min read | Webster Bank Being a high earner not rich yet (HENRY) may come with financial challenges. When coupled with the responsibility of raising a child with developmental disabilities, you might need thoughtful financial planning even more. Here are a few strategies that may help you save for retirement while managing your child’s well-being. Craft a Comprehensive Financial Plan A comprehensive financial plan should take into account both your short-term and long-term goals. Begin by assessing your current financial situation, including income, expenses, and debt. Then, factor in the additional costs associated with raising a child with developmental disabilities, such as therapy, specialized education, and medical expenses. Creating a detailed financial roadmap provides clarity and can help you allocate your resources. Consider consulting with a financial professional who specializes in working with families facing special needs. They may provide personalized insights for your specific circumstances. Establish a Special-Needs Trust One essential element of financial planning for families with children with developmental disabilities is establishing a special-needs trust (SNT). An SNT is a legal instrument designed to provide financial support for a person with a disability without jeopardizing their eligibility for government benefits like Medicaid and Supplemental Security Income. Through an SNT, you may contribute funds for your child’s future care and well-being while safeguarding their access to essential government assistance programs. Work with an attorney experienced in special needs planning so the trust meets your child’s specific requirements. Retirement Contributions As a HENRY, take advantage of retirement savings opportunities to build a robust financial foundation. Contribute to your employer-sponsored retirement plan, like a 401(k) or 457, and capture any available employer match. Additionally, consider contributing to an individual retirement account (IRA) or Roth IRA to diversify your retirement savings further. While balancing the financial demands of raising a child with developmental disabilities, consistently contributing to retirement accounts helps build a nest egg for your future. Automate your contributions to make saving a seamless part of your financial routine. Explore Government Assistance Programs Research government assistance programs that may provide financial support for families with children with developmental disabilities. You may be eligible for state or federal programs that offer financial aid, respite care, or other types of assistance. Plan for the Unexpected Review and update your insurance policies to determine if your family has adequate insurance coverage for unexpected events. Life insurance, disability insurance, and long-term care insurance are crucial components of a comprehensive risk management strategy. Insurance coverage may help your family in the event of unforeseen circumstances. Work with an insurance professional to assess your coverage and make necessary adjustments based on your evolving needs. Look for Community and Support Networks Building a community of support is invaluable for HENRYs navigating the complexities of raising a child with developmental disabilities. Connect with other parents facing similar challenges, join support groups, and seek out resources within your community. Shared experiences may offer practical insights and emotional support, helping you navigate the joys and challenges of parenting a child with special needs. title: What Makes a Leadership Legacy Last? Reflections on Clemens Scholz’s 26-Year Career at Novanta

body_text: By Johannes Tschepe, Senior VP Global Sales & Marketing When people talk about successful leaders, they often focus on business results or growth milestones. Those achievements matter, but the most enduring leaders leave behind something greater. As Vice President, Marketing Clemens Scholz retires after 26 years in medical technology, I have been reflecting on what made his career so impactful. His accomplishments were significant. He helped grow a leading Advanced Surgery business and championed lean operating principles, advancing technologies that strengthened our market position and supporting strategic growth initiatives across the organization. His influence extended beyond operational and product innovation into long-term business strategy, where he helped identify and evaluate opportunities that continue to shape our future direction. What distinguished Clemens, however, was not only what he accomplished, but how he accomplished it. Clemens studied mechanical engineering and medicine and wrote his Ph.D. thesis in Biomedical Engineering. He brought a rare ability to connect technical, clinical and business perspectives. He could quickly understand complex challenges and identify meaningful opportunities, helping teams find practical solutions. That combination of knowledge and curiosity made him particularly effective in identifying emerging opportunities and seeing potential where others might not yet see it. Equally important was his commitment to integrity. Throughout his career, Clemens consistently chose the path that aligned with his principles, even when it was not the easiest option. That authenticity earned the trust and respect of employees throughout the organization. Employees always knew where they stood with Clemens. He was honest and approachable, creating an environment where people felt empowered to contribute and innovate. As the organization grew, he remained deeply connected to everyone and genuinely interested in their success. Innovation was equally central to his leadership style. Clemens encouraged employees to challenge assumptions and explore new ideas, always thinking beyond conventional solutions. His curiosity and willingness to invest in people helped create a culture where innovation could thrive. What stands out most is the balance he maintained between driving results and supporting people. While leading substantial business growth and technological advancement, he never lost sight of the individuals behind those achievements. Employees remember a leader who knew them personally and encouraged them, consistently bringing positive energy to the workplace. Clemens’ influence also extended beyond business performance. Through volunteer efforts and charitable initiatives, he demonstrated that leadership is ultimately about serving others and making a meaningful difference. As our industry continues to evolve, the lessons from Clemens’ career remain as relevant as ever: Prepare thoroughly. Stay curious. Support innovation. Respect diverse perspectives. Lead with integrity. Never lose sight of people. These principles shaped Clemens Scholz’s extraordinary 26-year career and will continue to influence the teams and leaders that follow. That is what makes a legacy last.
